card.text: Explore Bacchus in 3D with its published radar shape model.

introduction.text: Bacchus is a small near-Earth asteroid with a prominent central indentation in its radar-derived shape. Explore its original shape and radial heights. The grid marks unavailable surface imagery. This is the paper’s conservative single-lobe working model, not a uniquely resolved shape. Radar data cover about half a rotation, and the degree of bifurcation remains uncertain. The pole is uncertain by tens of degrees; the sidereal period is 15.0 ± 0.2 hours. No resolved optical surface map is supplied.

shape.title: Radar shape model
shape.summary: A radar model based on half a rotation. Its shape and pole are uncertain; gray grid: no surface imagery.

elevation.title: Shape-derived radial height
elevation.summary: Radar-model height relative to a 315 m sphere. Half a rotation was observed; the shape is uncertain.
